emptyNoFile: Open a board .md with the “Open as tugtile” command.
laneActionsAria: Lane actions (rename / insert / sort / stash / delete…)
splitNoNeed: Only one line — nothing to split.
editLost: Tile no longer exists — edit not saved.
confirmDeleteLane: This lane has {0} tiles. Delete the whole lane?
confirmArchiveLane: Stash all {0} tiles in this lane?
noLaneToRestore: tugtile: no lane to restore into — create a lane first
externalModified: tugtile: this file was changed elsewhere — reloaded to avoid overwrite (this step was not saved)
backupFailed: tugtile: backup failed — write cancelled to protect your data
boardSettingsDesc: Affects only this board (saved with the board file). Blank = follow the global default.
migrateBtnDesc: Remove obsidian-kanban markers so this board is tugtile-native. One-way.
migrateConfirm: Upgrade this board to tugtile’s own format? It will no longer open in obsidian-kanban, and kanban-only settings will be dropped.
setEnterBehaviorDesc: shift-enter = Enter submits (CJK friendly); enter = Enter newline
setLinkDailyDesc: Write date as @[[..]] linking to the daily note
setTagActionDesc: What clicking a tag does — search the whole vault, or filter just this board.
settingsDesc: These are global defaults; a board’s own settings of the same name take precedence.
gShowCheckboxesDesc: Show a checkbox at the top-right of each tile (toggles - [ ] / - [x])
gHideCountDesc: Don’t show the tile count in the lane header
gResponsiveBoardDesc: On a narrow pane, the board reflows into a single vertical stack.
gLaneWidthDesc: Width of every lane — all lanes line up evenly
gTableDensityDesc: Vertical breathing room for each table row
gInsertToolsDesc: Which insert buttons show (code, link, date, time)
gEnterSubmitDesc: On: Enter submits, Shift+Enter newline (CJK-friendly default). Off: Enter newline, Shift/⌘+Enter submits
gPrependDesc: Default adds at the bottom; enable to add at the top
gRelativeDateDesc: Show “today / tomorrow / in N days” on tile dates
gDateDisplayDesc: moment-style tokens: YYYY / MM / DD (default YYYY-MM-DD)
gArchiveWithDateDesc: Prepend **YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm** to the title when stashing
gArchiveHeadingDesc: Heading text for a new stash (archive) section (e.g. Archive, 封存).
gResetDesc: Restore the above global settings to defaults
cmdConvertToBoard: tugtile: convert current note to board
boardCreated: Board created: {0} (rename it in the file explorer)
mtInsertToolsDesc: Which insert buttons to show (code / link)
mtDefaultEditor: Make marktile the default Markdown editor
mtDefaultEditorDesc: Off by default. When on, .md files open in marktile instead of Obsidian's editor (board files too — hop to tugtile with its button). Reload Obsidian to apply; turn off anytime to restore the native editor.
mtSettingsDesc: marktile opens any .md note in the tile-family editor. Choose which toolbar buttons appear (uncheck all to hide the toolbar entirely), or make marktile your default Markdown editor.
mtModesPickDesc: Which modes the view-cycle button rotates through. At least one stays on.
mtModesMinOne: Keep at least one view mode.
mtSeasonedColorDesc: Color each markdown token (headings, bold, code, links) with its own hue instead of a single accent tint.
backupDesc: tugtile snapshots this board to _tugtile-backups/ before the first change each session, and reloads if the file is edited elsewhere — a bad edit or a sync clash never loses your work.
backupEmpty: No backups yet — one is made automatically before this board's first change each session.
backupRestoreConfirm: Replace the current board with this backup? Your current state is backed up first, so this is reversible.
backupRetentionDesc: How many backups to keep per board; the oldest are removed beyond this (-1 keeps all).
familyMarktileDesc: A Markdown editor where the markers never hide and headings grow — same engine, same feel as the card editor here.
familyTugtileDesc: Turn your Markdown notes into a card board you can tug to reorder. Reads your existing boards.
familyHave: You already have the full tile family.
keyboardHint: Tip: focus a card (Tab or click), then use the arrow keys to move it — up/down within a lane, left/right across lanes.
